title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck is setting up an abstract 'universal cochain complex'. The aim is to describe the category of flasque, ∂-perfect semi-simplicial k-modules (next page) by a universal property.

The abstract set-up. Let C be a k-additive category, meaning an additive category with a ring map k → End(id_C). Let C^• = (C^0 →d^0→ C^1 →d^1→ …) be a cochain complex in C. Two axioms are imposed:
(a) Hom(C^i, C^j) is 0 unless j ∈ {i, i+1}. It is k·id for j = i and k·d^i for j = i+1. In particular d^{i+1}d^i = 0 is forced.
(b) Every object of C is a finite direct sum of the C^i.

Now let A be the full subcategory on the C^i. It is not additive, but it is k-linear. In fact A is the k-linear path category of the quiver 0 → 1 → 2 → … modulo the relations d∘d = 0. C is then its additive envelope, i.e. finite matrices over A. Existence of such (C, C^•) is therefore 'immediate by abstract construction'.

Concrete model. Take bounded chain complexes L_• of k-modules (degrees ≥ 0) that satisfy:
1° they are acyclic;
2° L_n and Z_n are free of finite type;
3° L_n = 0 for n large.
Then B_{n-1} = Z_{n-1} is free and L_n ≅ Z_n ⊕ Z_{n-1}. So L splits as a finite sum of disk complexes K(i) = (k →id→ k) concentrated in degrees i+1 and i.

K(i) is the free chain complex on one generator in degree i+1. Hence Hom(K(i), K(j)) = K(j)_{i+1}. This is k when j = i (identity) or j = i+1 (the map d^i with (d^i)_{i+1} = id_k), and 0 otherwise. The composite d^{i+1}d^i lands in K(i+2)_{i+1} = 0. So (a) and (b) hold.

Role in the manuscript. The next page states the payoff (Prop. 1). For any k-additive B, k-additive functors C → B are the same as k-linear functors A → B, which are the same as cochain complexes in B, via F ↦ F(C^•). The flasque ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules, which are sums of Δ̂^i ⊗ k, furnish another model of the same C. Hence a 'dévissage' of such semi-simplicial objects into cochain complexes, i.e. a Dold–Kan-type statement for semi-simplicial modules, used afterwards to transport multiplicative (divided-power) structures, as on the previous page.
errors: Gap regarding the marginal word 'karoubienne'. With the condition 'L_n, Z_n free', the model category is generally not idempotent-complete when k has nontrivial idempotents or non-free projectives (e.g. summands such as P⊗K(i) with P projective non-free). The abstract additive envelope of A is likewise not Karoubian in general. Projective of finite type (as hinted in the next page's margin) or k local/PID is needed for 'karoubienne'.
Minor: the abstract existence is called 'immediate'. It requires specifying the composition law (d^{i+1}∘d^i = 0, and the k-bilinear identity compositions). This is forced, but it is not stated.

ideas.what: Category of cochain complexes in B identified with k-additive functors out of the additive envelope of the k-linear category A = k[0→1→2→…]/(d²=0); C^• as the universal cochain complex
ideas.modern_name: Complexes as representations of the A_∞ quiver with relations d²=0 / free additive category on a complex (Yoneda-type universal property)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (representation theory of quivers with relations; Mitchell's 'rings with several objects', 1972)

ideas.what: Realization of the additive envelope as contractible bounded complexes of finite free modules, i.e. finite sums of disk complexes K(i), with Hom(K(i),K(j)) computed by the free-generator property
ideas.modern_name: Disk complexes D^{i+1} as free/projective generators in the projective model structure on Ch(k)

ideas.what: Planned use: identify the same abstract category with flasque ∂-perfect semi-simplicial k-modules (sums of Δ̂^i⊗k), yielding a Dold–Kan-type dévissage for semi-simplicial modules via comparison of k-linear categories
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan-type equivalences via Morita/Karoubi-envelope comparison of linear categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lack–Street, 'Combinatorial categorical equivalences of Dold–Kan type' (JPAA 2015); Pirashvili and others for variants

missed.claim: Grothendieck proves Dold–Kan-type statements by axiomatizing a k-additive category generated by a 'universal cochain complex' (Hom pattern k, k·d, 0) and exhibiting several models (disk complexes; flasque ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules). This is essentially the method later systematized by Lack–Street (2015), here applied to the semi-simplicial case around 1975–76.
missed.quote: Hom(C^i, C^j) ≃ { 0 si j≠i,i+1 ; k si j=i, base id_{C^i} ; k si j=i+1, base d^i }
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the 'categorical Dold–Kan via additive envelopes' viewpoint. The semi-simplicial (½-simplicial) variant combined with divided-power multiplicative structures is less standard in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine, correct set-up: the additive envelope of the d²=0 quiver category and disk complexes as its model. Its interest lies only in being an early instance of the axiomatic 'universal complex' approach to Dold–Kan-type equivalences, applied to semi-simplicial modules.

'{+de k-modules [?]+}' appears to be the superscript insertion 'k' before 'complexes de chaînes', not a duplicate 'de k-modules'.
In the definition of A, the reading 'les Hom_A sont des k-modules libres [?]' is uncertain. The image suggests 'les Hom_A sont des k-modules, les compositions [?] sont k-bil.'
Left margin contains degree labels ('degré 0', 'degré i', 'degré i+1') with a sketched vertical diagram of the disk complexes, not text.
